findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed bar soda gun to be soiled with black mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed in house dressing to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and dressing was discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed multiple coolers to be missing thermometers. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and thermometers were added to cooler units. Ensure a thermometer is available in all cooler units.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed multiple flies to be present within facility. Discussed with PIC, Orkin will be contacted. Ensure no pests are present within facility, inspector will follow up on 10/8/26.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Observed pizza prep cooler lids to be needing replaced. Discussed with PIC, lids will be replaced. Ensure proper lids are added to unit to ensure equipment meets manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the gap in between prep cooler and prep cooler lids to be soiled with food splash/debris in multiple coolers. Discussed with PIC, prep coolers will be cleaned. Ensure non-food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash/debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed caulking to be needing replaced at triple sink in dish room. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced as needed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed a member of staff wash hands without using a barrier to turn off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing, and employee rehashed hands. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off hand sink faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed employee bare hand a cooked pizza from oven to tray. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper bare hand food handling practices. Ensure any ready to eat foods are properly handled by employees.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed staff to be date marking items in multiple coolers, however inspector observed date marking to be missing on multiple TCS items throughout multiple coolers and walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking practices. Dates were placed on all TCS items, ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed a bag of chicken to be thawing near pizza oven. Discussed with PIC, education on proper thawing practices was provided, chicken was moved to a pan under running water. Ensure facility is properly thawing TCS items to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed multiple in use rags to not be stored in sanitizer buckets between use. Discussed with PIC, education on sanitizer rags was provided. Rags were all moved to sanitizer buckets testing at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure any in use rag is being stored in a sanitizer solution to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed in use pizza cutter to be resting on a soiled rag on counter. Discussed with PIC, pizza cutter was put through wash, rinse, and sanitize process and stored in an approved location. Ensure in use utensils are stored in cleaned and sanitized locations.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: Ice cream scoop is observed to be stored in the ice cream with the handle touching the food. Store the scoop properly according to one of the methods listed in the code reference that follows:
FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a large quantity container holding some ranch dressing with no date marking and a same size container of Caesar dressing with the date 3-30 on it. The Ranch was discarded. Also quantities of pasta salads made in house are observed to have no date marking. Facility is closed Mondays so the pasta salads were fresh yesterday.  Yesterdays date was placed on the items immediately. Take care to properly date mark items and discard items in 7 days. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the counter at the wait station. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizing solution between uses every time. Do not let wet wiping cloths sit on surfaces. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed unopened cans of personal drinks stored randomly in cold holding units mixed with items for service to the public. Inspector suggests providing a bus tub or other solid container in which to store employee food items. The container can go on the floor of the walk in under the shelves. Items were moved to the walk in.
Two different phones and a speaker were observed on surfaces in the kitchen. The phones were located next to sheet pans that were going to be put into the oven and heated to well above 165F. These are still food related items and should be protected from personal items such as phones and speakers. The phones were moved to surfaces were food related items are not going to be stored. 
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.
